Berkshire's more affordable Class B stock 3% this year, trailing the benchmark S&P 500 index's 13% year-to-date gain. data.title: UBER Stock Soars Despite Analysts' Price Target Cuts after Q2 Earnings
data.description:
Shares in ride-hailing giant Uber Technologies (UBER) jumped by 6% on Friday afternoon. This came as analysts rushed to slash their price targets on the stock, pointing to drag from Uber's autonomous vehicle (AV) push. Uber reported mixed Q2 2026 earnings on Wednesday, August 5, with its third-quarter outlook falling short of expectations. However, most analysts kept their Buy rating on the stock.

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions

Uber Stock Defies Price Target Cuts

Responding to the results, the following analysts kept their Buy ratings but trimmed their price targets as follows:

  • Cantor Fitzgerald's Deepak Mathivanan cut his price target from $98 to $90. This new target suggests about 20% upside.
  • DA Davidson's Tom White lowered his price target from $107 to $100. The new target still suggests about 34% upside.
  • Bernstein's Nikhil Devnani slashed his price target from $110 to $95. The new target implies about 27% upside.
  • Susquehanna's Shyam Patil trimmed his price target from $110 to $90.

For the quarter ended June 30, Uber's revenue came in at $14.2 billion, up by 12% from a year ago. However, this slightly missed expectations of $14.24 billion. By contrast, the earnings per share of $0.81 matched estimates.

Uber Is 'in Cruise Control, Just Needs an AV Driver'

Defending his rating, Mathivanan noted that the Q2 results overall showed "a strong quarter" and healthy finances. He noted that Uber's gross bookings topped Wall Street estimates by 1%. The figure grew by 24% from a year ago to $58 billion.

However, the analyst said he expects UBER stock to remain under pressure until investors become more sure of how the AV game will play out. Notably, Uber has outlined plans to invest $10 billion to support its AV push over the next several years.

Mathivanan noted that Uber is "in cruise control, just needs an AV driver." This suggests that the mobility company looks healthy and only needs to convince investors about its AV strategy.

"AVs are currently live on Uber in 7 cities with up to 15 expected live by year-end, the analyst noted. "Meanwhile, AV partners have committed about 120,000 vehicles to the Uber network over the coming years."

Is Uber Stock a Good Buy Right Now?

Across Wall Street, Uber's shares continue to enjoy a Strong Buy consensus rating from analysts. This is based on 28 Buys and three Holds assigned over the past three months.

In addition, the average UBER price target of $103.96 implies about 39% upside (see UBER stock forecast here).

data.title: Dow Jones Today: DJIA Edges Higher after Jobs Report Eases Rate Hike Odds
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is trading higher on Friday after the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) published July's jobs report.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

During the month, nonfarm payrolls decreased by 23,000, well below the consensus expectation of 80,000 additions. Furthermore, May and June's payrolls were revised lower by a combined 103,000 jobs.

The BLS also said the unemployment rate dropped to 4.1%, below the estimate of 4.2% and down from 4.2% in June. That appears good on the surface, although what actually happened is that the labor force participation rate fell to 61.4%, its lowest level since February 2021. In other words, the labor force shrank as fewer people sought work.

"This is a bleak jobs report," said Navy Federal Credit Union Chief Economist Heather Long. "The U.S. labor market is stalling again and that is going to make the Federal Reserve's job harder and life for job seekers rough."

Following the report, the odds of a 25-bps rate hike at the September 16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting fell to 41.9% from 55%, according to the CME FedWatch tool. That provided a supporting hand to stocks, as higher rates reduce the present value of future earnings.

The report also makes the Fed's job more difficult. The central bank must now grapple with raising rates to tame inflation or lowering rates to stimulate the labor market. Of course, leaving rates unchanged is also on the table and is the most likely outcome at the September FOMC. Investors will receive a key inflation update next week when the BLS releases July's Consumer Price Index (CPI).

The Dow Jones is up by 0.16% at the time of writing.
data.author: Eddie Pan

data.title: Can SpaceX Stock Reach $800? Here's What This Top Analyst Expects
data.description:
SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) stock is staging an impressive comeback, jumping about 13% on Friday and bringing its two-session gain to around 20%. One likely reason is that a potentially negative catalyst hanging over the shares is finally in the rearview mirror. SpaceX's first post-IPO lockup expired Thursday, making more than 900 million restricted shares eligible to trade and removing at least some of the uncertainty surrounding the event.

SPCX has a long & short ETF? Explore SPCM & SPCG

The rebound offers some relief after a difficult stretch since SpaceX went public. Despite Friday's surge, the shares remain about 38% below their post-IPO high, leaving plenty of ground to recover. Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale, who ranks among the top 3% of Wall Street analysts, thinks the longer-term opportunity extends far beyond simply reclaiming those previous highs.

Gesuale views SpaceX as much more than a rocket and satellite company, describing it as "one of the defining industrial infrastructure companies of the 21st century." At the core of his thesis is the convergence of cheaper access to space and rapidly expanding AI infrastructure, which he believes could open entirely new markets for SpaceX.

"Industrialized access to orbit and AI are driving the most significant infrastructure convergence since the advent of the Internet," Gesuale argues. In his view, SpaceX could ultimately create an infrastructure layer spanning transportation, communications, computing, manufacturing, and energy, giving the company opportunities well beyond its existing businesses.

The analyst goes further, comparing SpaceX's potential importance with some of the infrastructure breakthroughs that transformed earlier economic eras. "We believe SpaceX is building the foundational platform for the next generation of industrial capacity," Gesuale said.

SpaceX's latest quarterly performance only strengthened that conviction. The company exceeded Gesuale's expectations, while its growing AI operations gave him further reason to think his current forecasts could ultimately prove conservative. Management has moved its internal timeline for reaching $1 trillion in annual revenue forward by one year, to 2030. That revenue target is twice the amount Gesuale currently models for the year.

"We continue to have conviction in our thesis and see our forecasts as biased significantly higher in the near and long term," the analyst explained, adding that the difference between his projections and management's framework leaves "considerable optionality for upside with execution."

Starship represents a crucial part of that argument. Gesuale calls operationalizing the launch system "the critical path to the SpaceX investment thesis," making improvements in launch frequency particularly important. Following the progress demonstrated by Flight 13, the analyst believes the program is beginning to move toward the faster and more repeatable cadence required for commercial operations.

Gesuale is encouraged by what he is seeing, arguing that recent progress represents "a meaningful step" toward proving the Starship model. Combined with Starlink's expanding network, rising AI computing capacity, and continued work on orbital infrastructure, successful Starship commercialization could substantially widen SpaceX's addressable opportunity.

All of that comes down to a very bullish call on the stock. Gesuale assigns SPCX shares a Strong Buy rating and a Street-high $800 price target. From current levels, that implies a whopping 517% upside. (To watch Gesuale's track record, click here)

The rest of Wall Street is bullish as well, although not nearly as optimistic as Gesuale. SPCX earns a Moderate Buy consensus rating, based on 24 Buys, 5 Holds, and 2 Sells. The $229.54 average price target implies about 78% upside from current levels. (See SPCX stock forecast)

data.title: SpaceX's (SPCX) Next $740 Billion Opportunity Isn't Rockets or AI
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) may have another huge growth opportunity outside of rockets and artificial intelligence. In its IPO materials, the company estimated that Starlink Mobile could serve a global market worth about $740 billion. That does not mean SpaceX expects to make $740 billion in revenue. Instead, it means that is the size of the mobile market the tech company believes Starlink could eventually compete in.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

High conviction SPCX bulls now have this Tradr ETF

And recent comments from SpaceX suggest that the firm wants Starlink to become much more than a backup service for areas without normal cell coverage. The biggest change is that SpaceX appears to want to compete more directly with traditional wireless companies. In fact, President Gwynne Shotwell recently said that SpaceX plans to build more ground-based infrastructure so Starlink can become a "true mobile service."

She also said that the company expects to win some customers away from AT&T (T), Verizon (VZ), and T-Mobile (TMUS). Interestingly, SpaceX previously agreed to buy 65 MHz of wireless spectrum from EchoStar (ECHO) for $19.6 billion in November 2025 in order to work toward this goal. For reference, spectrum is simply the range of radio frequencies that wireless companies use to send phone signals. By owning more of it, SpaceX would have more control over how Starlink Mobile operates.

SpaceX Already Has a Starting Point

Meanwhile, SpaceX already has a starting point. Through its partnership with T-Mobile, compatible phones can connect to Starlink satellites when normal cell service is unavailable. However, becoming a full wireless provider would require much more equipment and ground infrastructure.

That is also where the biggest challenge comes in. Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile have spent decades building nationwide networks and control much more spectrum. Because of that, analysts believe that SpaceX may need more partnerships or acquisitions instead of trying to build an entire network from scratch.

Still, the opportunity helps explain why Starlink could become much bigger than just satellite internet. SpaceX estimates that there are about eight billion connected mobile devices worldwide outside of China and Russia. Therefore, even winning a small share of that market could create a large source of recurring revenue.

data.title: Comcast Stock (NASDAQ:CMCSA) Notches Up With Private Wireless Network
data.description:
We know that entertainment giant Comcast (CMCSA) has been pivoting away from entertainment to focus on its technology side. And recently, Comcast made quite a step forward by rolling out its private wireless network, one of which it recently installed at the Smartlink company headquarters. The news was reasonably welcome to investors, who gave Comcast shares a fractional boost in Friday morning's trading.

Putting a private wireless network in at Smartlink is a good look for Comcast. Smartlink, as it turns out, handles wireless infrastructure operations for a range of carriers and tower companies. The move was intended to take the current legacy distributed antenna system (DAS) infrastructure and instead bring in a complete Citizens Broadband Radio Service (CBRS) private network.

With this, Smartlink now has better access to coverage—no more gaps cropping up in unusually-shaped portions of the building or places where coverage otherwise did not reach—as well as a secure private network. This gives Smartlink better access to smart-building applications as well, which can deliver some noteworthy results in terms of cost savings and quality of life.

A Bad Day for Universal Studios Hollywood

Meanwhile, anyone who went to Universal Studios Hollywood recently is being advised to check their immunization status, particularly against measles. Because, as it turns out, someone who had measles recently spent the day at the theme park, instead of staying home, and out of everybody's way.

Word from the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health says that the visitor in question hit the park on July 26, and was there pretty much the full day, from 10 in the morning until nine at night local time. Given that measles viruses can remain airborne for up to two hours, reports note, that makes most anyone who was at the park that day potentially susceptible. And with over 2,300 infections reported in the United States this year so far, it is clear that measles cases are on the rise.
